title: The no-go theorem: P1, P2 and P3 cannot all hold

statements.text: No theory can satisfy irreducible history dependence (P1), local-state sufficiency (P2) and causal efficacy (P3) together for any pair of realizations, $\neg \exists \alpha, \beta \, [P1 \wedge P2 \wedge P3]$. By P1 the pair has equal states and inputs but different consciousness. P2 then gives equal futures and P3 different ones, a contradiction.

sources.quote: A theory cannot jointly satisfy irreducible history-dependence (P1), local state sufficiency (P2), and causal efficacy (P3) for any pair of realizations
We prove the theorem by contradiction.
